subject: Geopolitics
title: Fishing Wars
description: Learn Fishing Wars in one minute.

hook.text: Chinese fishing fleets of 300 boats anchor off the Galapagos Islands. Ecuador's navy can barely respond.

buildup.text: Fishing is a resource war fought at sea. Overfishing near home pushes industrial fleets into other nations' waters.

discovery.text: China's distant-water fleet is the world's largest: 3,000 vessels. It depletes stocks off West Africa and South America.

twist.text: Poor nations lack navies to patrol their EEZs. Illegal fishing steals protein from people who need it most.

climax.text: Fishing disputes have triggered naval standoffs between Japan and Taiwan, UK and France, and Argentina and Spain.

punchline.text: Fish are invisible — until they're gone and nations fight.

quiz.question: Why does illegal fishing disproportionately harm poor nations?
options: Poor nations eat more fish than wealthy ones
They lack navies to patrol and enforce their EEZ boundaries
Wealthier nations subsidize their fishing fleets more
